response: Yes, there can be discordance between clinical pathologists and clinicians when reporting and interpreting red blood cell morphology. This discordance may arise from differences in terminology, classification, and interpretation of morphological findings, as well as varying levels of expertise and experience. Clinical pathologists may use specific terminology and classification systems to describe red blood cell morphology, which may not be familiar to clinicians. Additionally, clinicians may not always understand the clinical significance of certain morphological findings, leading to potential misinterpretation or underutilization of the information. Effective communication and collaboration between clinical pathologists and clinicians are essential to ensure accurate interpretation and appropriate clinical decision-making based on red blood cell morphology results.
